sources.entry: Memos - Knowledge base that works with a SQLite db file. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker/Go

summary.one_liner: Memos is an open-source, self-hosted note-taking app that organizes everyday thoughts into a personal, tag-based timeline.
summary.what_it_does: Memos lets you write short or long notes in Markdown, with each memo stamped to the day it was written. Tags connect related notes across days so you can revisit a topic or find something you wrote earlier. Data is stored on your own server, and the README says you choose which memos stay private, which are shared with family and friends, and which are published on the web. Shared spaces let several people write alongside each other while each keeps their own memos. The README also mentions a Web Clipper for Chrome and Firefox that saves pages, selections, and images as Markdown with a source link, a Telegram bot called Memogram, and an API and MCP server for connecting scripts and AI tools.
use_cases: saving web pages and clippings as notes
sharing selected notes with family or friends
connecting scripts or AI tools to a notes store
how_to_run: With Docker installed, run: docker run -d --name memos -p 5230:5230 -v ~/.memos:/var/opt/memos neosmemo/memos:stable
Open the web address and create the first account.
All data is kept in ~/.memos, so back up that folder.
Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and plain binary options are described in the deployment guide (not reproduced in the README).
notable: Timeline-based notes where each memo is tied to the day it was written, with tags linking across days
Per-memo privacy control: private, shared with family and friends, or published on the web
Shared spaces where multiple people write while keeping their own memos
Web Clipper extension for Chrome and Firefox saves pages as Markdown with source links
API and MCP server for integrating with scripts and AI tools
caveats: Upgrading from releases before v0.31.0 requires running v0.31.0 first, per the README
Other deployment methods are only referenced in the external deployment guide
